fields.title: Resources and risks: what must be known before launch
fields.keyTakeaway: A project relies on three things: who participates, what it depends on, and what can go wrong. A risk without an owner and a trigger indicator is unmanaged — it's just waiting to happen.
fields.checkQuestion: Risk: "the vendor might delay the API." What is missing in this phrasing?
fields.blocks/0/text: Key node question: **what resources are needed for the changes?**
fields.blocks/1/subtitle: One page instead of a twenty-page charter
fields.blocks/1/items/0: **Why** — what is the goal and how will we know we achieved it.
fields.blocks/1/items/1: **Who** — team, stakeholder, who signs off on results, whose approval is required.
fields.blocks/1/items/2: **Scope and out-of-scope** — the second half is more important than the first.
fields.blocks/1/items/3: **Dependencies** — external deadlines, third-party systems, procurement, access permissions.
fields.blocks/1/items/4: **Risks and assumptions** — things we take on faith without proof.
fields.blocks/2/subtitle: A phrasing that leads to action
fields.blocks/2/items/1: **Probability and impact** — roughly, in three levels; precision isn't needed here.
fields.blocks/2/items/2: **Trigger indicator** — what we will notice first; without it, the risk is spotted after the fact.
fields.blocks/2/items/3: **Response** — mitigate, transfer, accept, or prepare a workaround. Decided in advance.
fields.blocks/3/text:
Poor: "Scanner vendor might delay the SDK."

Actionable phrasing:
Event — new scanner SDK won't be out by February 15.
Probability medium, impact high: without it, we can't assemble the release for Gastronom, deadline March 1.
Trigger indicator — if there is no beta by February 1, they won't make it in time.
Response — build a fallback in advance: manual code entry, two weeks of work, start January 20 in parallel.
Owner — Igor.

On February 1, there was no beta. The fallback was already being written; the release went out on February 26.
fields.blocks/4/text: A timeline chart shows well what cannot start before something else ends: migration after integration, enablement after release. For routine product work, it creates an illusion of precision more often than it helps.
fields.blocks/4/title: Gantt charts are useful strictly where hard dependencies exist
fields.blocks/5/text: Schedule estimates are ranges presented as numbers. Treat the plan as a dependency discovery tool rather than a date commitment: commitments are made by counting backward and adding buffer.
